seo.title: Common Multiples of 4 and 6 - LCM 12 Math Speed Challenge
seo.metaDescription: Click all common multiples of 4 and 6 on a 100-tile grid. Practice least common multiple (LCM) concepts and avoid the common product trap.
seo.intro: A common mistake students make is multiplying 4 by 6 to get 24, assuming 24 is the smallest shared multiple. In reality, because 4 and 6 share a common factor of 2, their least common multiple (LCM) is 12. Consequently, all common multiples of 4 and 6 are multiples of 12 (12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96). This speed clicker teaches students to spot shared multiples efficiently.
seo.howToPlay: Locate and click every number that is a multiple of both 4 and 6. Correct selections turn green with checkmarks. Incorrect tiles flash red and penalize 2 seconds from the clock. Find all 8 common multiples to win.
seo.teacherNotes: Use this example to contrast multiplying two numbers (4 x 6 = 24) with finding their actual least common multiple (LCM = 12).

faq.q: Why is the LCM of 4 and 6 equal to 12 rather than 24?
faq.a: Because both 4 and 6 share the prime factor 2. Using prime factors: 4 = 2^2, 6 = 2 x 3. The LCM takes the highest power of each prime: 2^2 x 3 = 12.
